captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a heavy-duty downhill freeride crankset. It features a wide, cylindrical bottom-bracket shell housing a continuous rotating spindle, with two oversized, rectangular black crank arms attached at opposite 180-degree angles. A large, circular black bash-guard outer ring is mounted on one side, supported by a four-spoke spider. Rectangular platform pedals are mounted via thin axles to the ends of each crank arm, allowing independent continuous rotation.
captions.instruction: Generate a 3D model of a downhill freeride crankset with a wide bottom-bracket shell, two oversized crank arms, and a bash-guard outer ring. Ensure the spindle and crank arms rotate continuously relative to the bottom bracket, and each platform pedal rotates independently about its axle spindle.
captions.factory: Create a fixed base representing the bottom bracket shell using a cylinder primitive. Construct a rotating spindle and crank assembly using cylinders for the axle and crank arm ends, combined with box primitives for the main arms. Model the bash-guard as a thin cylinder/disc with a patterned four-spoke spider. Model each pedal as a box with a cylindrical mounting spindle. Establish continuous joint connections between the bottom bracket and the crank assembly, and between the crank arms and each pedal.
